concepts.note: The maximum efficiency of any heat engine between reservoirs at T_H and T_C is η = 1 - T_C/T_H.
concepts.title: Carnot efficiency

concepts.note: The cycle alternates isothermal expansion and compression with adiabatic expansion and compression.
concepts.title: Reversible cycle legs

concepts.note: No engine operating between the same two reservoirs can exceed the reversible Carnot efficiency.
concepts.title: Carnot theorem

concepts.note: Irreversible processes reduce work output, motivating the later concept of entropy.
concepts.title: Reversibility and maximum work

subtopics.note: Carnot idealized a reversible heat engine operating between two reservoirs and showed that its efficiency depends only on their temperatures, η = 1 - T_C/T_H. The cycle consists of two isothermal and two adiabatic reversible processes.
subtopics.title: Carnot cycle

concepts.note: Mechanical work churned water and raised its temperature, establishing the mechanical equivalent of heat in the 1840s.
concepts.title: Joule's paddle-wheel experiment

concepts.note: Joule estimated about 4.2 J per calorie, linking work and heat quantitatively.
concepts.title: Mechanical equivalent of heat

concepts.note: The change ΔU depends only on initial and final states, not on the path.
concepts.title: Internal energy as a state function

concepts.note: The first law expresses conservation of energy for thermodynamic systems, including heat and work.
concepts.title: Energy conservation

subtopics.note: Heat and mechanical work are equivalent forms of energy, and the internal energy of a system is a state function: ΔU = Q - W, with work done by the system. Joule's paddle-wheel experiments provided quantitative support.
subtopics.title: First law of thermodynamics

concepts.note: Heat cannot flow spontaneously from a colder to a hotter body without external work.
concepts.title: Clausius statement

concepts.note: No cyclic engine can convert heat from a single reservoir entirely into work.
concepts.title: Kelvin-Planck statement

concepts.note: Clausius introduced entropy as a state function whose change measures reversible heat transfer divided by temperature.
concepts.title: Entropy

concepts.note: For any cyclic process ∮ δQ/T ≤ 0, with equality only when reversible.
concepts.title: Clausius inequality

subtopics.note: Clausius and Kelvin stated the impossibility of certain spontaneous heat-flow and engine processes. Clausius later introduced entropy in 1865, yielding ΔS ≥ ∫ δQ/T, with equality for reversible processes.
subtopics.title: Second law of thermodynamics

concepts.note: Molecular speeds follow f(v) ∝ v² exp(-mv²/2kT) in thermal equilibrium.
concepts.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution

concepts.note: Clausius introduced the average distance a molecule travels between collisions.
concepts.title: Mean free path

concepts.note: Each quadratic degree of freedom contributes ½kT to the average energy in classical thermal equilibrium.
concepts.title: Equipartition theorem

concepts.note: Kinetic theory relates viscosity, thermal conductivity and diffusion to molecular collisions.
concepts.title: Transport coefficients

subtopics.note: Maxwell derived the molecular speed distribution f(v) ∝ v² exp(-mv²/2kT) and, with Boltzmann, connected macroscopic gas properties to microscopic collisions. Clausius had earlier introduced the mean free path.
subtopics.title: Kinetic theory of gases

concepts.note: The right-hand side sums changes in f from binary molecular collisions.
concepts.title: Collision integral

concepts.note: Boltzmann assumed pre-collision velocities are statistically uncorrelated, introducing irreversibility.
concepts.title: Molecular chaos (Stosszahlansatz)

concepts.note: Boltzmann showed his H functional decreases monotonically, connecting microscopic dynamics to entropy growth.
concepts.title: H-theorem

concepts.note: Loschmidt's reversibility and Zermelo's recurrence objections exposed tensions between microscopic reversibility and macroscopic irreversibility.
concepts.title: Reversibility and recurrence objections

subtopics.note: Boltzmann's integro-differential equation describes how a one-particle distribution evolves under external forces and binary collisions: ∂f/∂t + v·∇_r f + (F/m)·∇_v f = (∂f/∂t)_coll.
subtopics.title: Boltzmann equation

concepts.note: A macrostate's entropy counts the number W of microscopic configurations consistent with it.
concepts.title: Microstates and macrostates

concepts.note: S = k log W links thermodynamic entropy to statistical multiplicity.
concepts.title: Boltzmann entropy formula

concepts.note: The constant k ≈ 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K was introduced by Planck in 1900.
concepts.title: Boltzmann constant

concepts.note: Equilibrium corresponds to the overwhelmingly most probable macrostate, explaining entropy increase statistically.
concepts.title: Second-law interpretation

subtopics.note: Boltzmann related entropy to the number W of microscopic configurations compatible with a macrostate, S = k log W. Planck later introduced the constant k and gave it Boltzmann's name.
subtopics.title: Statistical entropy

concepts.note: An isolated system with fixed energy is described by a uniform distribution over accessible microstates.
concepts.title: Microcanonical ensemble

concepts.note: A system in contact with a heat bath has P ∝ exp(-H/kT), yielding the Helmholtz free energy.
concepts.title: Canonical ensemble

concepts.note: A system exchanging energy and particles with a reservoir uses a grand partition function and chemical potential.
concepts.title: Grand canonical ensemble

concepts.note: The normalization Z encodes the statistical sum from which thermodynamic observables follow.
concepts.title: Partition function

subtopics.note: Gibbs formulated statistical mechanics through ensembles of microscopic states, with canonical probabilities P ∝ exp(-H/kT) and thermodynamic quantities derived from partition functions such as F = -kT ln Z.
subtopics.title: Gibbs ensembles
